title: 按键的上拉与下拉：别让输入悬空
summary: 起始电路里的按键少了一个电阻，输入是浮空的。补上 10 kΩ 下拉（按下读 1），再用内部上拉接第二个按键（按下读 0）。
concepts: 高 / 低电平有效 active-high / active-low
description: 按键 SW1：3V3 → SW1 → GPIO_IN1，再经 R1（10 kΩ）下拉到 GND，高电平有效。按键 SW2：GPIO_IN2 → SW2 → GND，靠内部上拉，低电平有效。参考答案 SW1 用 GPIO34（只能输入、没有内部上下拉），SW2 用 GPIO33。

en.title: Pull-ups and pull-downs: never leave an input floating
en.summary: The button on the starting board is missing a resistor, so its input floats. Add a 10 kΩ pull-down (pressed reads 1), then wire a second button with the internal pull-up (pressed reads 0).
en.description: Button SW1: 3V3 → SW1 → GPIO_IN1, pulled down to GND through R1 (10 kΩ): active-high. Button SW2: GPIO_IN2 → SW2 → GND with the internal pull-up: active-low. The reference uses GPIO34 for SW1 (input only, no internal pulls) and GPIO33 for SW2.
compare: - Both released: IN1 reads **0** (R1 pulls it to 0 V), IN2 reads **1** (internal pull-up to 3.3 V).
- Both pressed: IN1 reads **1** (3.3 V) and R1 carries 3.3 V / 10 kΩ ≈ **0.33 mA**; IN2 reads **0** and the internal pull-up passes 3.3 V / 45 kΩ ≈ **73 µA** (out of the pin into the button).
- IN2 switched to a plain input (pull-up forgotten): released, IN2 **floats** — the same mistake as the starting circuit.
If a reading jumps around or shows as floating, check that input has its pull resistor and the right pin mode.

measurements.ask: Both buttons released: the IN1 pin to GND
measurements.explain: The input draws almost nothing, so R1 drops nothing: IN1 sits at 0 V and reads 0.

measurements.ask: Both released: the IN2 pin to GND
measurements.explain: The internal pull-up takes it to 3.3 V; it reads 1.

measurements.ask: Both pressed: the current in R1 (the pull-down)
measurements.explain: The button puts 3.3 V straight across R1: 3.3 V / 10 kΩ ≈ 0.33 mA, drawn for as long as it is pressed, which is why a pull resistor can't be too small.

measurements.ask: With IN2 changed to a plain input (no pull-up) and the button released, IN2 reads
measurements.explain: A CMOS input is > 10 MΩ; with the button open nothing ties it to a level — exactly the starting board's GPIO34 problem (GPIO34–39 have no internal pulls, so they need external ones).
choices: undefined: the pin floats and the reading wanders with leakage and noise
always 0: an unconnected pin is 0 V

hints: SW1's other side already goes to GPIO34; put a 10 kΩ from the same column to GND.
SW2: one side to a second GPIO, the other straight to GND, no resistor.
Select the board and set the second GPIO to IN pull-up. GPIO34–39 can't do that; use a pin such as GPIO33, GPIO25 or GPIO26.
tests: Both released: IN1 reads 0 (pull-down), IN2 reads 1 (pull-up)
Both pressed: IN1 reads 1, IN2 reads 0
Pull-up forgotten (plain input): IN2 floats when released

cards.title: A floating input
text: The board is already wired: button **SW1** has one side on **3V3** and the other on **GPIO34**, a plain input.
**Click the board** and watch GPIO34's reading. Then **hold SW1 down** with Select / use, and let go.
What does it read pressed? Released? What do the **diagnostics** on the right say?

cards.title: Tie the input to a rope
text: - An input draws almost no current. With the button released GPIO34 is connected to nothing, so leakage and noise decide its voltage — the reading wanders. This is **floating**.
- The fix: tie it to a level with a resistor. A **pull-down** goes to GND: released it reads 0; pressed, the button (about 0 Ω) easily overrides the resistor and it reads 1.
![](fig:pulldown)
- For as long as the button is pressed, a current flows in the resistor:
- With numbers: with 4.7 kΩ, $I = \frac{3.3}{4700} ≈ 0.0007$ A, about 0.7 mA. Too small a resistor wastes power, too large picks up noise; buttons usually get 4.7–10 kΩ.
- A **pull-up** is the mirror image: the resistor goes to 3.3 V, the button to GND, and pressed reads 0. Most pins have a pull-up of about 45 kΩ inside the chip — choose IN pull-up and it is there.

cards.title: Add the pull-down, then a second button
text: - From the column where SW1 meets GPIO34, put a **`10 kΩ`** to GND.
- Then a second button, **SW2**: one side to another GPIO (GPIO33, say), the other straight to GND, no resistor.
- **Click the board** and set SW2's pin to **IN pull-up**. GPIO34–39 have no internal pulls, so don't use them for SW2.
- Press **Check my circuit**, then measure both input voltages and the current in R1.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **An input needs a definite level**: without a pull-up or pull-down, the pin floats when the button is released.
- **To 3V3 + pull-down → pressed reads 1; to GND + pull-up → pressed reads 0.** The second is more common: one part fewer, and a wire touching the case cannot short the supply.
- Mechanical buttons **bounce**: for a few milliseconds they open and close several times. Debounce in the program with a delay, or add an RC filter.
- A real-circuit catch: the ESP32's GPIO34–39 have no internal pulls, so they need external ones; GPIO0, 2, 5, 12 and 15 set the boot mode at power-up, so keep buttons and pull resistors off them.

tests.name: 都松开：IN1 读 0（下拉），IN2 读 1（上拉）
忘了开上拉（普通输入）：松开时 IN2 浮空

compare: - 都松开：IN1 读 **0**（R1 把它拉到 0 V），IN2 读 **1**（内部上拉到 3.3 V）。
- 都按下：IN1 读 **1**（3.3 V），R1 里流过 3.3 V / 10 kΩ ≈ **0.33 mA**；IN2 读 **0**，内部上拉电流 3.3 V / 45 kΩ ≈ **73 µA**（从引脚流出到按键）。
- 把 IN2 改成普通输入（忘了开上拉）：松开时 IN2 **浮空**——这就是起始电路的错误。
读数在跳或显示浮空时，看那个输入是不是缺了上拉 / 下拉，或引脚模式没设对。

measurements.ask: 两个按键都松开：IN1 引脚对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 输入几乎不取电流，R1 上没有压降：IN1 被拉到 0 V，读 0。

measurements.ask: 都松开：IN2 引脚对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 内部上拉把它拉到 3.3 V，读 1。

measurements.ask: 都按下：R1（下拉电阻）里的电流
measurements.explain: 按键把 3.3 V 直接加在 R1 上：3.3 V / 10 kΩ ≈ 0.33 mA。按下期间一直在耗电，所以下拉不能太小。

choices: 不确定：引脚浮空，读数随漏电和干扰乱跳
一直是 1：输入默认是高电平
一直是 0：没接东西就是 0 V
measurements.ask: 把 IN2 改成普通输入（不开上拉），按键松开时 IN2 读到的是：
measurements.explain: CMOS 输入阻抗 > 10 MΩ，按键断开时没有任何东西把它拴在一个电平上——这正是起始电路里 GPIO34 的问题（GPIO34–39 没有内部上下拉，必须外接）。

hints: SW1 的另一边已经接到 GPIO34；从同一列再插一个 10 kΩ 到 GND。
SW2：一边接第二个 GPIO，另一边直接接 GND，不用电阻。
选中开发板，把第二个 GPIO 设成「输入 上拉」。GPIO34–39 做不到，请用 GPIO33、GPIO25、GPIO26 这类引脚。

cards.title: 一个悬空的输入
text: 面包板上已经接好：按键 **SW1** 一边接 **3V3**，另一边接 **GPIO34**，引脚是普通输入。
**单击开发板**，看 GPIO34 那一行的读数。再用「选择 / 操作」**按住 SW1**，然后松开。
按下时读到什么？松开时呢？右边的**诊断**怎么说？

cards.title: 给输入拴一根绳子
text: - 输入几乎不取电流。按键松开时，GPIO34 什么都没接，它的电压由漏电和干扰决定——读数乱跳，这叫**浮空**。
- 解决办法：用一个电阻把它“拴”在一个电平上。**下拉**电阻接 GND：松开时读 0；按下时按键（约 0 Ω）轻松压过电阻，读 1。
![](fig:pulldown)
- 按下的整段时间里，电阻上都流着电流：
- 代入数字：用 4.7 kΩ 时，$I = \frac{3.3}{4700} ≈ 0.0007$ A，约 0.7 mA。电阻太小白白耗电，太大又容易被干扰，按键常用 4.7–10 kΩ。
- **上拉**反过来：电阻接 3.3 V，按键接 GND，按下读 0。大多数引脚芯片里自带一个约 45 kΩ 的上拉，选「输入 上拉」就有了。

cards.title: 补上下拉，再接一个按键
text: - 从 SW1 接 GPIO34 的那一列，插一个 **`10 kΩ`** 到 GND。
- 再插一个按键 **SW2**：一边接另一个 GPIO（例如 GPIO33），另一边直接接 GND，不用电阻。
- **单击开发板**，把 SW2 用的引脚设成**「输入 上拉」**。GPIO34–39 没有内部上下拉，所以 SW2 别用它们。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**，然后测两个输入的电压和 R1 的电流。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **输入一定要有确定的电平**：没有上拉或下拉，按键松开时引脚就浮空。
- **接 3V3 + 下拉 → 按下读 1；接 GND + 上拉 → 按下读 0。** 后者更常见：少一个零件，导线碰到机壳也不会短路电源。
- 机械按键会**抖动**：按下的几毫秒里通断好几次。程序里要延时消抖，或者加一个 RC 滤波。
- 真实电路里的坑：ESP32 的 GPIO34–39 没有内部上下拉，必须外接；GPIO0、2、5、12、15 在上电时决定启动方式，别在上面挂按键和上下拉。

caption.text: 下拉：松开时 R1 把 IN1 拉到 GND（读 0）；按下时按键把 IN1 接到 3.3 V（读 1），电流 I 流过 R1。

i18n.en: Pull-down: released, R1 pulls IN1 to GND (reads 0); pressed, the button connects IN1 to 3.3 V (reads 1) and a current I flows in R1.
